title_content.content: Improving outlook in 2H26; strong shareholder returns

paragraph_content.content: PO: 101.60 HKD | Price: 92.25 HKD

BofA preview – revenue +LSD-MSD driven by overseas and 2B (partly offset by likely domestic 2C declines), core NPAT -MSD on cost and FX losses, and reported NPAT up YoY after factoring in investment gains as well as impairment charges. We reiterate Buy rating due to 1) improving outlook in 2H26, 2) diversification into 2B and overseas to support long-term growth and valuation, and 3) solid shareholder returns (100% payout ratios including share buyback, with potential upside from investment gains),

Midea guides for MSD-HSD revenue growth and largely stable core margins in FY26. We estimate that its 1H26 run rate is tracking behind schedule, but see potential for a catch-up in 2H26. 1) 2C. China/overseas was +SD/flat in 1Q26, and estimated to be -MSD/+MSD in 2Q26. We expect stronger China/overseas in 2H26, due to an easier base (demand pull-forward by trade-in subsidies in China and overseas rush orders amid trade wars in 1H26) and continued strength of OBM (expected to be +teens). 2) 2B. We estimate 2B growth to be +MSD in 1H26 and expect similar or faster trends in 2H26. Historically, 2B enjoyed >10% growth but FY26 growth could be below-trend given the drag from Industrial Solution (components for 2C) and a high base of Intelligent Building. Energy Storage and Kuka should outperform the 2B average. 3) Core margins. We expect margin expansion in 2H26, due to an easier base, recent corrections of plastic cost and very stringent cost and SG&A control.

title_content.content: Potential investment gains to offer dividend upside

paragraph_content.content: We expect Midea to book mark-to-market fair value changes from its investment in memory companies since 2Q, and see likely meaningful gains in 2Q/3Q26. Some of these gains may likely be offset by impairment charges. While the investment is subject to a one-year lock-up period, we expect Midea to monetize the stake following the lock-up expiry in 2027. We also see the potential for the associated proceeds to be returned to shareholders through special dividends or other shareholder return initiatives.

paragraph_content.content: Appliances

Midea is a leading technology-driven global provider of Smart Home Solutions (2C) and Commercial & Industrial Solutions (2B). It is the world's largest home appliance company. Its subsidiary KUKA is one of the world's big 4 industrial robotics companies. Midea Electric was listed on Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 1993 and Midea Group listed in 2013 by merging with Midea Electric. Midea was also listed on Hong Kong Stock Exchange in Sept 2024.

We rate Midea as Buy for three reasons. 1) Midea's 2C+2B & globalization support steady growth against China's macro softness. 2) Midea is a proxy to China stimulus given trade-in subsidies now and optionality on more subsidies in 2025. 3) Midea's consistent track record, quality management and solid shareholder returns make it a consumer core holding in A & H-share market, in our view.

paragraph_content.content: BofA GLOBAL RESEARCH

Our PO for Midea-H is HK$101.6, which is derived from a 50/50 blend of PE and DCF. Our DCF-based value is HK$115, based on 11.1% WACC, 0.9x beta, and 2% terminal growth. Our P/E-based value is HK$88.2, derived from 13x 2026E P/E, which is largely on par with HK listed China consumer peers and global home appliance peers, and at a 30% premium to HK-listed white goods peers on Midea's industry leadership and more stable growth outlook. We also assume HKDCNY exchange rate of 0.9.

Risks are a likely industry down-cycle in 2026 after the lapping of trade-in subsidies, tariffs, home appliance demand, execution risks of 2B expansion, commodity prices, industry competition, overseas regulations and tariffs, FX risk, and key personnel risk.

Our PO for Midea-A of RMB96 is based on a 5% premium to our Midea-H PO (HK$101.6), which is derived from a 50/50 blend of PE and DCF. Our DCF-based value is HK$115, based on 11.1% WACC, 0.9x beta, and 2% terminal growth. Our P/E-based value is HK$88.2, derived from 13x 2026E P/E, which is largely on par with HK listed China consumer peers and global home appliance peers, and at a 30% premium to HK-listed white goods peers on Midea's industry leadership and more stable growth outlook. We derive our target A/H premium based on the average of two factors. 1) Historically, the average of A/H premium for Haier Smart Home, Midea's closest peer, has been c.10%. 2) In 2025 YTD, Midea's own A/H premium has narrowed to largely nil. We also assume HKDCNY exchange rate of 0.9.

Risks are a likely industry down-cycle in 2026 after the lapping of trade-in subsidies, tariffs, home appliance demand, execution risks of 2B expansion, commodity prices, industry competition, overseas regulations and tariffs, FX risk, and key personnel risk.

paragraph_content.content: FUNDAMENTAL EQUITY OPINION KEY: Opinions include a Volatility Risk Rating, an Investment Rating and an Income Rating. VOLATILITY RISK RATINGS, indicators of potential price fluctuation, are: A - Low, B - Medium and C - High. INVESTMENT RATINGS reflect the analyst's assessment of both a stock's absolute total return potential as well as its attractiveness for investment relative to other stocks within its Coverage Cluster (defined below). Our investment ratings are: 1 - Buy stocks are expected to have a total return of at least 10% and are the most attractive stocks in the coverage cluster; 2 - Neutral stocks are expected to remain flat or increase in value and are less attractive than Buy rated stocks and 3 - Underperform stocks are the least attractive stocks in a coverage cluster. An investment rating of 6 (No Rating) indicates that a stock is no longer trading on the basis of fundamentals. Analysts assign investment ratings considering, among other things, the 0-12 month total return expectation for a stock and the firm's guidelines for ratings dispersions (shown in the table below). The current price objective for a stock should be referenced to better understand the total return expectation at any given time. The price objective reflects the analyst's view of the potential price appreciation (depreciation).
Investment rating Total return expectation (within 12-month period of date of initial rating) Ratings dispersion guidelines for coverage cluster
Ratings dispersions may vary from time to time where BofA Global Research believes it better reflects the investment prospects of stocks in a Coverage Cluster.

INCOME RATINGS, indicators of potential cash dividends, are: 7 - same/higher (dividend considered to be secure), 8 - same/lower (dividend not considered to be secure) and 9 - pays no cash dividend. Coverage Cluster is comprised of stocks covered by a single analyst or two or more analysts sharing a common industry, sector, region or other classification(s). A stock's coverage cluster is included in the most recent BofA Global Research report referencing the stock.
